newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia plans to buy nine aircraft by 2001.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia plans to buy nine aircraft by 2001.

text.p: Tunisia plans to buy nine aircraft between 1997 and 2001, including seven to replace part of the fleet of the national airline Tunis Air, an official report showed on Monday.

A sectorial report for the 9th development plan for 1997-2001 obtained by Reuters says the two other planes would be for the privately-owned charter company Nouvelair and the domestic airliner Tuninter.
The document says Tunis Air was to replace its ageing seven Boeing-727s and two Boeing-737s.

Total investment in the air transportation sector between 1997 and 2001 were put at 589 million dinars, including the purchase of the nine planes and the extension of Tunisia's main airports, the report said.
Tunis Air's fleet includes 24 planes from Airbus and Boeing models, among them nine it has bought during the last five years.

The state-controlled company has a capital of 53 million dinars. In 1995, it sold 20 percent of its capital for 32 million dinars in the biggest sell off in Tunisia's privatisation programme so far. An additional sell off is planned for 1997.
Tunis Air shares on the Tunis Stock Exchange were last priced at 23 dinars. ($=1.08 dinar)
